supportedSubstanceClasses: neutral or weakly sorbing organic chemicals under screening-level multimedia assumptions
release scenarios that can be approximated as regional mass loading into air, water, soil, or sediment compartments
deterministic assessor-review and benchmark workflows that require transparent concentration-only outputs
unsupportedSubstanceClasses: metals and metal species requiring speciation-aware fate treatment
nanomaterials or particulate systems requiring size-resolved transport behavior
strongly ionizing chemistries where screening partition and persistence assumptions are likely unstable
assessments dominated by transformation products, food-chain transfer, or explicit intermedia transfer kinetics
requiredInputs: media-specific capacity defaults or governed overrides
media-specific half-life defaults or governed overrides
coreAssumptions: The runtime emits regional concentration surfaces rather than dose, exposure, or risk values.
Each release medium is represented as a single screening compartment with governed capacity defaults.
Finite-duration first-order decay is applied over the declared release duration and any post-release elapsed time.
Steady-state mode reports the end-of-duration screening concentration rather than an infinite-time equilibrium.
Only treatment assumptions explicitly marked as pre_release_global are numerically applied before release; all other treatment assumptions remain provenance-only.
Reference mass balance does not add explicit advective clearance or intermedia transfer terms.
reviewNotes: Use for concentration-only screening support, benchmark demonstrations, and downstream suite handoff preparation.
Review unsupported runtime parameters before treating outputs as more than screening indicators.
Escalate to richer model families when multiple complex media interactions dominate the decision context.
reference_mass_balance.applicabilityNote: Reference mass balance is appropriate for transparent deterministic screening workflows inside the declared Fate MCP boundary.

supportedSubstanceClasses: screening-level organic chemical releases where a single-compartment concentration estimate benefits from an explicit residence-time or clearance term
regional air, water, soil, or sediment releases where first-order degradation plus first-order advective clearance are an acceptable deterministic simplification
review workflows that need a concentration-only output with calculation traces for both degradation and residence-time loss terms
unsupportedSubstanceClasses: metals and metal species requiring speciation-aware fate treatment
nanomaterials or particulate systems requiring size-resolved transport behavior
assessments requiring explicit intermedia mass transfer, plume dynamics, or spatial hydrodynamics
cases where residence-time defaults are too coarse to represent local transport conditions credibly
requiredInputs: media-specific capacity defaults or governed overrides
media-specific half-life defaults or governed overrides
media-specific residence-time defaults or governed overrides
coreAssumptions: The runtime emits regional concentration surfaces rather than dose, exposure, or risk values.
Each release medium is represented as a single screening compartment with governed capacity defaults.
Finite-duration first-order degradation and first-order advective clearance are combined into one total loss constant per medium.
Steady-state mode reports the end-of-duration screening concentration rather than an infinite-time equilibrium.
Only treatment assumptions explicitly marked as pre_release_global are numerically applied before release; all other treatment assumptions remain provenance-only.
reviewNotes: Use when a screening workflow needs a governed residence-time clearance term in addition to first-order degradation.
Treat the family as experimental and compare it against the corrected reference family before using it in decision-facing review materials.
Escalate to richer model families when spatial hydrodynamics, drainage structure, or intermedia exchange dominate the question.
advective_screening_mass_balance.applicabilityNote: Advective screening mass balance is a non-default experimental family for deterministic concentration-only screening with governed residence-time clearance.

adapter_stub.applicabilityNote: Adapter stub exists to validate integration seams, not to support scientific decisions.

scenario context for region, timing, and provenance anchoring

external_result_adapter.applicabilityNote: External-result adapter is suitable when imported concentration surfaces need governed normalization and reviewable provenance, not when Fate MCP should replace the source engine.
